    Lumina Kingdom¶

    "The old empire's bones are everywhere. We sit on its heart." — King Gustal, on the throne of the Lumina Kingdom

    A kingdom on the Lumina Continent, built on the ruins of the ancient Lumina Empire — a once-great empire of the beastmen, and the greatest power the continent has ever known. The current kingdom occupies the site of the old imperial capital, carries its name, and dreams of reclaiming its legacy.

    The Old Lumina Empire¶

    Rise (1729 BGD — Golden Age)¶

    From approximately 1729 BGD to 1134 BGD, the Lumina Empire dominated the continent. At its height, it controlled:

    • 70% of the Lumina continent
    • Cattos island
    • Large portions of the Tuba Continent

    It was a civilization of architects, scholars, and warriors — built and ruled by a civilized, intelligent beastmen people, the first true empire to unify the disparate tribes and species of ancient Lumina. In those days the beastmen were as capable of empire as any race of humans: its founding emperor, Kaelor I, was a beastman. Its cities were marvels. Its roads still run beneath the jungle. Its statues — weathered but standing — can be found across the continent, half-consumed by forest.

    The Shadows Within¶

    The Shadows had been inside the Empire since its founding. Every institution, every ministry, every military command — seeded with homunculi, guided by Hybrian agents. They did not want the Empire to rule. They wanted it to fall. This was Phase One of the Shadow plan: Infiltration — seed the institutions, wait, and when the moment is right, make them fall. The Lumina Empire was their first great test.

    The Fall — Luminous XII¶

    The empire's collapse began with its greatest king.

    Luminous XII, called "the Architect," was a legendary beastman ruler — builder of cities, conqueror of lands. Brilliant, visionary, and utterly blind to the rot within. In a campaign on Tuba, the Shadows engineered a war with the Goblin King. A conflict that should have been a trivial border skirmish became a catastrophic defeat through sabotage, corrupted intelligence, and whispered advice in the right ears.

    Luminous XII lost the battle. The defeat was not merely military: his brother Hoelio died in the fighting.

    Luminous XII returned to the capital shattered. He had no heirs. He had no will to continue. Consumed by shame, he took his own life.

    The year was 1134 BGD. The empire died with him. The Pax Lumina — six centuries of stability — ended in fire and blood.

    The Collapse¶

    Without Luminous XII's legitimacy, the succession collapsed. Rival claimants tore the empire apart from within. The centralized state that had held the continent together for six centuries dissolved in a generation.

    And then the beastmen — the empire's own people — broke.

    The fall destroyed their pride. Slowly, over generations, the civilized beastmen of Lumina returned to savagery: the roads untraveled, the cities abandoned, the writing forgotten. In the chaos, beastmen kin from Marti Continent crossed the sea and joined the splintering tribes — but no invading power finished the empire. The beastmen simply forgot what they had been.

    The civilization that had produced Luminous XII's statues crumbled back into jungle and memory.

    For over a thousand years, Lumina was a continent of ruins.

    Beastmen — Post-Collapse¶

    The beastmen of Lumina today — the Gigas Tribe, the Maoma Tribe, the scattered warbands — are the descendants of the empire that collapsed. They are fierce, tribal, and honor-driven. Physical strength is the measure of worth. Raiding and inter-tribal warfare are the norm. Their culture resembles the beast races of ancient legend: warriors first, everything else second — a far cry from what their ancestors were.

    Historically, people know it: the beastmen of old were more civilized and intelligent, and they built empires as readily as any race of humans. Some say the fall of the empire destroyed their pride and made them humble. The old Lumina Empire's ruins are everywhere — and the beastmen walk past them, only half-remembering that those stones were their own making.

    Religion — Lumism¶

    The Lumina Kingdom follows Lumism — the imperial cult of the old Lumina Empire's figures, blended with animism and a reverence for the jungle animals. Its believers hold that the kingdom must return the Lumina Empire and bring back the old ways of the beastmen — restoration is not ambition among the devout, it is duty. For all that, the kingdom remains highly tribal and decentralized, with a slow, genuine push toward modernization.

    The Current Lumina Kingdom¶

    The modern Lumina Kingdom occupies the same location as the old imperial capital. It inherits the name — and the ambition.

    King Gustal¶

    The current ruler, King Gustal, is a human monarch who claims descent from the scattered imperial bloodline. His claim is disputed by scholars but accepted by his subjects. Gustal is no Luminous XII — he is not an architect or a conqueror. But he is ambitious.

    Ambitions¶

    The Lumina Kingdom intends to retake lost lands and eventually reform the Lumina Empire. This is not secret. Gustal speaks of it openly. The other powers of Lumina — especially Gigas — listen carefully.

    Military¶

    Lumina Kingdom is strong enough to rival Gigas. It is not yet strong enough to defeat them. The balance of power on the continent is fragile: two powers, each claiming to be the rightful heir to continental dominance, watching each other across the jungle.

    The Ruins¶

    Across the Lumina continent, the old empire's remains are visible:

    • Weathered statues of forgotten kings, carved from white stone now stained green by moss.
    • Broken aqueducts that once carried water to cities of a hundred thousand.
    • Road foundations, perfectly straight, now buried under centuries of topsoil.
    • Imperial inscriptions in a script that modern Lumina scholars can barely read.

    The past is everywhere. The present is still catching up.

    Shadow Connection¶

    See also: Shadows, Hybrians, Audio Chapter 5 — The Old Lumina Empire

    The fall of the Old Lumina Empire was not merely political decay. It was the Shadows' first documented large-scale operation — proof that infiltration at institutional scale could topple even a six-century superpower. The pattern established here — seed agents, wait generations, engineer a crisis, let the collapse look natural — would be refined and repeated across Ge'or for millennia.
